best_variant: bm25_tight (fully measured). The hybrid 'ledger' variant leads by +2.1 S on the first 40 dev questions only (83.2 vs 81.1): a provisional result that needs full dev and dev200 sweeps.
failure_patterns: The baseline numbers are for generic 'naive'. The generic 'hybrid_rr' bar on multi was never measured: the shared model server was backlogged all session. Reference from the task: S about 73 on an 80-question all-type sample.

No shared vocabulary, so the gold session is never packed. Examples: 'How many projects have I led' against 'I presented a poster on my research'; 'How many years will I be when Rachel gets married' against 'I'm 32, so I'm in my 30s'. The age pattern fires on the second one, but the session ranks below the many Rachel/married sessions and falls out of the budget.

Gold turn sits in a packed session but is not picked inside it. Examples: 'visited The Art Cube on 2/15' for museums/galleries (neither word appears); 'my black Fender Stratocaster electric guitar' for musical instruments; on dev200, the health-devices question loses gold session #90.
Unreachable or odd gold turns cap ATR at about 0.98: an assistant turn ('Congratulations on raising $250') that repeats the user's own turn, and 'No, that's all for now. Thanks for your help!'.

Abstention is weak (AUC 0.74 dev, 0.61 dev200). Unanswerable questions usually miss one facet ('headphones and the iPad', '30-gallon tank'), and dev windows like 'museums in December' cannot be checked because the window never engages on dev.

On test, the packs include every decoy alongside the true instances: friends' purchases ('My friend Valentina bought...'), declined buys ('tried on ... decided not to buy'), 'skipped buying'. Filtering them is left to Reactor through the hint. Count questions that are really a stated, updated number ('How many ceramic pieces am I putting in the class show?') need a 'latest statement wins' rule.
core_requests: Model server throughput: every hybrid/rerank sweep on the machine sat at 0% CPU for 60+ minutes while core.precompute dev ran. Make precompute yield to interactive requests (or batch across clients), or announce when the dev/dev200/test embedding caches are complete.
List the exact core.pack.message_chars(q, passages, hint) signature in CONTRACT.md. My Round-0 draft assumed (question, hint, passages); it is now fixed in the lens.
harness.failures: mark each gold turn as included or missed using included_turns saved in per_question.jsonl. My lens stores debug['inc'] as a stopgap.
Save cite_plan in harness.audit's test_packs.jsonl so citation behaviour on test-style decoys can be reviewed.
Final multi citations should come from cite_plan, not from every pack session: the pack holds 20-30 sessions for recall while gold has 2-5. Agent B asks for the same.
next_ideas: Run full dev and dev200 sweeps of 'ledger' (hybrid) and 'ledger_rr' (with rerank). On 40 dev questions 'ledger' scored S 83.2 vs 81.1 for bm25_tight on the same questions, with ALL 1.0. Keep bm25_tight as the fallback that needs no model server.

Score sessions by their best fact-like topic sentence (topic hit + first-person event verb + number) instead of unit-level RRF, so chatter-heavy test topics (orchids, swimming) rank instance sentences first.

Code-side ledger as a note passage (id=None): date | session | sentence for in-window, own, non-negated topic sentences with a number. Set 'computed' only for clean sums, and only after Reactor spot checks.
For count questions on test, cite every in-window clean instance session instead of the 0.8 score-fraction rule. Dev cannot tune this, so it needs test-like synthetic checks.
KU-like multi questions ('these days', 'current plan', 'am I putting'): order by recency, keep the newest 3 statements, and hint that the latest value wins.
Borrow agent B's facet guarantee: give the best session of each side of an 'X and Y' question a reserved slot. It also feeds the missing-facet abstention signal.

failure_patterns: No word overlap in event-less 'topic' questions (BM25 only). 'What kitchen appliance did I buy 10 days ago?': the gold turn is 'I just got a smoker today' on exactly the resolved date, and ATR is 0. Same for 'gardening-related activity two weeks ago' (tomato saplings) and 'business milestone four weeks ago' (signed a contract with my first client). Dense retrieval or the cross-encoder is needed. Near-date picks recover some of these but push decoys out of the pack, so the net gain is 0.

Gold sets that include every same-topic decoy session, so ALL=0 even with the answer in the pack. 'music event last Saturday' has 5 gold Saturday sessions; 'order of the six museums' gets 5 of 6; 'pair of shoes cleaned last month' has 5 gold sessions.

Order questions with sessions on the same day and restatements in later turns. 'Europe with family vs solo trip to Thailand': both sessions are dated 05/28, the gold turn is t10 and the pick is another turn. 'coffee maker vs stand mixer': the event dates appear only as 'about three weeks ago' or 'last month' in a sentence next to the picked one.

Unit conversion and vague durations give wrong computed values (HA=0): 'How many months ago did I book the Airbnb in San Francisco', 'weeks since I recovered from the flu when I went on my 10th jog', 'weeks accepted into the exchange program when ... orientation'.

Test audit: 'How many years did I serve as a firefighter?' has no events and goes to topic mode with abstain_p 0.1, although it is probably an abstain question. 'Montreal flat alerts -> lease' has correct relative dates ('tonight' and 'today') but scores below min_score, so computed is withheld.
core_requests: Model-server throughput: a fresh query embedding takes about 20 s while 12+ sweeps run. Precompute and cache embeddings for question texts and lens-parsed event phrases, or add a batched hx.dense_many(queries). Without it, dense and cross-encoder temporal variants cannot be evaluated inside the time box. The generic temporal baseline itself did not finish in over 60 min.
Pipeline: use cite_plan for temporal citations. CF1 is 0.97 on gap and order questions, against about 0.5 when every pack session is cited.
Router: send 'How many days apart/after/before ...' to temporal with high confidence (34 of 36 test temporal questions).

core.dates: adopt the holiday grammar ('a week before Black Friday'), 'the 22nd of April', M/D only after on/the/since, and future-penalised year inference. Also add a question-side resolver like a_calendar.question_window ('the Wednesday two months ago', 'in March and April', 'the past weekend').
Metric note: for order questions, ATR requires the exact gold turn, so a restatement in a later turn of the same session counts as a miss even though Reactor can answer from it.
next_ideas: Dense and cross-encoder in topic mode once the server is free: use q.question as the query (already cached by the generic baseline), rerank user units inside the time window with a time prior, then re-enable the near-date picks (near=2).
Topic-mode abstention: IDF coverage of the question terms by the best user unit, plus the 'only someone else did it' rule.
Relax min_score for picks with relative or session dates when the margin is large, so that 'tonight'/'today' test histories get a computed answer.
Order questions: when the picked sentence has no date, borrow a relative date from the next sentence of the same unit.
Weeks and months questions: put both 'N weeks (D days)' in the hint, and withhold computed when D/7 or D/30.44 is close to a rounding boundary.
Topic-mode CF1 is 0.43: cite the sessions inside the window plus the top topic session instead of the top-2 by fused rank.
Re-run the generic hybrid_rr baseline on dev and dev200 for temporal, and the round-0 dense variants (cal, cal_wide), once the server cache is warm.

failure_patterns: Newest value is a paraphrase with no question words, so neither BM25 nor admission of the dense top-3 reaches it. Dev: 'vehicle model I am working on' vs gold 'switched to a Ford F-150 pickup truck' (dense rank 6-7, BM25 rank 87). Test: the long-run update is only an assistant recap 'shifted to Sundays at 6:30 a.m.' (BM25 rank 142); variant pkv finds it.

A late low-coverage filler sentence with a same-kind value is promoted to newest by continuity or admission. Test UX team: 'Six people is solid for summer.' comes after 'now has eight people'. Dev200: '15 minutes every morning tidying' vs '4 weeks'. Test job title: 'lecturer's job' and 'role of a Marketing Director' come after 'now I am Director of Clinical Services'.

Wrong older session when the old value is repeated in several sessions. Dev family trip (Hawaii in two sessions), camera lens, Saturday wake-up time. PA stays 1, only citation precision is lost (CF1 0.5).
Test generator contradictions and multi-owner totals: 'My current rent is only 9,000, shared.' after the planted 22,000; 'Bjorn and I in total' needs one timeline per owner.
core_requests: Model server throughput: with ~15 concurrent sweeps a generic hybrid_rr KU dev sweep took 23 min, a cold dense query ~49 s and rerank40 ~11 s. Orphaned sweep workers (ppid 1) may still be sending requests; please clean them up and consider a queue per agent.

Move the lens's assemble() into core.pack as a pair-first group packer: priority groups of session -> units, full group then shorter prefixes, then neighbour fill. build_pack lets one chatty session use the whole budget and drop a cited session.
Router / generic path: use a_timeline.analyse() as an evidence-based KU detector. The submission should honour cite_plan for KU, since gold is always exactly 2 sessions.
Optional: HistoryIndex.value_units(regex), a cached list of units containing a value type, for the value-typed retrieval list (pkv).
next_ideas: Gate admission and continuity on all of the attribute's distinguishing key words, not just the head noun ('Six people' lacks 'UX team'), then combine with pkv (value-typed list) and accept only if dev200 holds.

Self-statement detector for picking the newest mention: prefer 'I am / my X is / now I / I switched' over requests or interest sentences. Track it with scratch_a/nsent_acc.py (newest sentence contains the answer: 48/72 dev, 13/22 dev200).
Sentence-level cross-encoder (B's rerank_texts request) used only to choose newest/older among the 3-4 strongest own mentions, keeping A's packing and hint.
One timeline per owner for 'X and I in total' with a summed computed value; apply relative updates ('2 more') in computed.
Abstention: combine A's missing-phrase signal with B's coverage-miss signal and calibrate on dev+dev200 together (only 10 unanswerable in total).

failure_patterns: The best-ranked turn is the gold turn in only 74/112 dev and 14/22 dev200 questions; the gold turn sits -8 to +8 turns away (for example Bandung Nasi Goreng -4, Radiation Amplified zombie +5, tea tree oil ratio +8). PA stays at 1.0 only because the whole best session is packed, so budgets of 5000 and 4000 lose 4% and 10% of PA (S 91.0 and 87.2).

Generic 'you recommended' questions in dev lost to cue sentences. For 'Mayo Clinic video you recommended', 'For YouTube creators, OBS Studio and XSplit are popular choices' beat the cue-less list item '"How to Sit Properly..." by the Mayo Clinic', so the wrong session was cited. Fixed by raising the cue floor to 0.7.

Ungated structure boosts pulled in decoy sessions. For 'type of beer for Seco de Cordero', 'For a reliable power adapter for Japan, I'd recommend the following' was lifted from another session and the gold turn fell out of the budget (PA 0.982). Fixed by boosting only sentences with recommendation shape >= 0.5 (head-noun or purpose match, a name, coverage >= 0.3).

Ordinal list items were computed from the wrong turn when the best turn moved: 'last venue in the list of Portland venues' returned 'Music festivals...'. Fixed: the item now comes from the first assistant turn in the best session, in ranking order, whose list has at least n items. Computed items are now right 6/6 on dev and 3/3 on dev200; harness HA reads 0.833/0.667 because of a metric artefact.

On test (qualitative), two picks were wrong before round 1: 'homebrew supply shop' (answer 'Peachtree Brew Supply'; 'homebrew' vs 'Brew' did not match lexically) and 'coworking space in Lisbon' (answer 'Heden in Baixa has a good day pass', with no Lisbon term). The compound-term match and shape boost fix both, so 25/25 test best sentences now look correct and 23/25 are quoted in the hint.
core_requests: harness.metrics HA for ssa/ssu: when the gold answer is a sentence ('The 27th parameter was Sound effects...'), compare computed by normalized containment before first_number; today a correct computed list item scores HA=0.

build_pack: when the budget cuts, keep the priority order of `ranked` (best turn first, session fill last) while still rendering chronologically; optionally add max_chars_per_session so a pack can hold 'best session whole + runner-up best turn only'.

Model server: per-agent queueing/priority, or a CONTRACT note that BM25-only is preferred where lexical retrieval saturates. The generic hybrid_rr baseline took 27.5 min for 112 ssa dev questions under load.
core.units._SENT: add an abbreviation guard (Dr., St., Mr.) so names like 'Dr. Vogel' are not split across unit boundaries. This matters for quoted-line hints.
next_ideas: Reactor A/B on about 10 test-style questions: recqs_cf7 (quoted 'likely line' hint) against the same lens with hint_mode=generic. Offline metrics can't see the quote; the test audit says the quoted line is right 25/25.

Better turn ranking, to cut chars without losing PA: a round score (assistant unit + preceding user turn, as in B's design) and the cross-encoder over the best session's turns only (about 10 pairs), then pack the best turn +-2 turns instead of the whole session, once turn@1 >= 0.95.
Dense purpose matching only for rec-style ties ('in Baixa' vs 'in Lisbon'): hx.dense(question, uids=units with shape >= 0.5), only a handful of vectors.

Quote gate: allow quoting when the runner-up has the same kind but a clearly different purpose (Coach Miriam vs Elena, margin about 1.1, currently suppressed), using purpose-overlap difference instead of the raw struct margin.
Integrator: since lexical-only already gets PA=1.0 and CF1=1.0 on ssa at about 250 ms/q with no model calls, route ssa to recqs_cf7 and keep the model server for other types.

failure_patterns: The second-unit session bonus (max + 0.1*second) favoured topical sessions over the side remark that holds the fact. On dev200 'How long was I in Japan for?', a session planning a future trip won over the past 'spent two weeks' statement. Removing the bonus and adding past/future tense agreement (variant nb3t0) fixed it.

The reranker prefers a related item over the asked one (open). In 'music streaming service I've been using lately', Netflix (logit -0.7) beat Spotify (-2.8). Owner and polarity features cannot separate them.

The gold fact is only a presupposition inside a request (open). For 'What breed is my dog?', the gold is '...suit a Golden Retriever like Max?' (logit -8.6) and the cited unit was 'What else should I get for my dog?' (-5.4). A -1 penalty for user wh-questions to the assistant was too small to flip it.

The round-0 classifier over-fired and tagged 12 of 64 dev gold units as decoys ('I'm thinking of visiting my sister Emily in Denver', 'thinking about my conversation with Sarah', 'my favorite artist's debut album'), which dropped them from the pack (PA -0.09 on dev200). Fixed: polarity is now judged per occurrence of the question verb and one affirmed occurrence wins; a possessor named in the question counts as the user's own.

Test audit: lexical abstention gates fired on a head word the user never writes ('AM intermediate frequency' vs 'AM IF ... 465 kHz'). This gave abstain_p 0.9 and an INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE hint even though the reranker was confident. Fixed by capping the gates at 0.3 when top logit > 0.
Name drift on test (the same cat is Fig, Sombra and Bica in different sessions) is still unresolved, so computed=Sombra is a guess.
core_requests: Answer-anchored citation: after Reactor answers, cite the pack sessions whose text contains the answer, falling back to cite_plan (ssu gold is always exactly 1 session).

A rerank cache-hit path or a priority queue in the model server: uncached cross-encoder pairs queue behind precompute and about 15 parallel sweeps (first dev sweep 646s, baseline dev200 1108s; about 10s once cached).
build_pack explicit-neighbour mode, or document window=0 plus explicit neighbour uids as supported (the nb* variants rely on it).
harness.audit: print pack.debug (top logit, qparse, decoys) next to each test pack.
Register the lens module in sys.modules before exec_module (Python 3.14 dataclass plus from __future__ annotations).
next_ideas: Value voting for name questions with drift: count the user's own affirmed mentions per value, prefer replies to 'What's her name?', break ties by recency; give a hint only when one value clearly leads, otherwise list the dated values.
Calibrate abstention (ab_bias, ab_temp, gate weights) on the abstain questions of all types; consider the generic all-roles top logit as a second prior (AUC 0.955 on dev200).
Modifier/domain agreement feature, e.g. 'music' streaming service vs Netflix.
Test cite_second_gap (already implemented): cite 2 sessions when the margin is small, since F1 pays off when p2 > p1/2.
Merge with lens B: B's declarative rewrites and session sweep for recall, plus A's owner/polarity/tense features and decoy notes for precision; both score in logit space.

failure_patterns: Dev and dev200 SSA are saturated. Packing the whole top session with 1 citation scores 92-93.3 S against a ceiling of about 93.3 at 5.5k chars, so variants (and lens A vs lens B, whose rec_bm25 scores 93.0/93.3) cannot be separated by the 2-point rule. Only test answer quality from Reactor can decide.

Turn-granular packing (top turns of the top session, about 4k chars) loses the gold turn when sibling turns repeat the entity or a long user brief outranks the assistant's answer. turns_rr reaches only PA 0.90. Examples: Bandung/Miss Bee Providore (gold_rank 6), Andy's shirt in the comedy script (gold_rank 20-28), Bajimaya construction year buried in a user-pasted case (gold_rank 12-15).

A budget cut inside a long top session drops the answer chunk while the gold turn still counts as partly included. DHL influencer budget $2,000 gives ATR=1 but AC=0, and the Fissionator zombie name is lost at 8k. Raising the cap from 8k to 10k fixes it.

Without the cross-encoder, session NDCG picks the wrong session once: the newspaper flower vase sealant question lost to an unrelated 'release flowers into the ocean' session. Rerank on top-40 of hybrid(raw question) restores SR=1.0.
A runner-up contrast unit inside the same budget pushes out top-session chunks: session8k scores 1.5 S below session8k1 on dev. It is only worth adding when the top session is small, as on test.
core_requests: Model-server throughput: rerank requests queued 10-30 s each behind the precompute and other agents, and the dev SSA baseline sweep took 30 min. Batch or prioritise small rerank calls, or precompute rerank(q.question, hybrid(q.question,k=100)) for all dev/dev200/test questions. My _rr variants use exactly that cache-compatible pool.

A build_pack priority mode: respect the order of `ranked` when the budget cuts, render chronologically, and include the whole session if it is <= N chars. I currently emulate this with window=0 and a hand-ordered uid list.
An --ablate-gold harness flag that drops the gold sessions from the index. Dev SSA has 0 unanswerables, so the AUC is undefined and abstain_p cannot be calibrated.
next_ideas: Keep the whole-session pack but trim non-best turns at sentence or paragraph level by rerank score. Target is about 4k chars with no PA loss, roughly +0.5 S.
Add the runner-up session's best unit only when the top session is under 3k chars (test-style injected sessions): near-miss contrast and recall insurance at about zero dev cost.
Have the integrator run Reactor on test-style samples to compare A rec_bm25 and B session10k1_rr. Dev metrics cannot separate them.

Gate the INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE hint note so it also requires the category word to be missing from the top session. This covers cue-less recommendations such as 'Heden ... has a good day pass' (Lisbon coworking, abstain_p=0.84 in the audit).

Test audit of session8k1: 11/12 hints quote exactly the purpose-matched first-person recommendation sentence. Keep the speech-act hint; the plain ablation ties on dev only because dev has no injected decoys.

failure_patterns: Plan beats past tense: dev200 'How long was I in Japan for?' cites the 'I'm planning a trip to Japan' session (logit 6.8) over the gold 'when I was in Japan ... spent two weeks' (2.1). The gold is in the pack (PA=1) but CF1=0.
Same slot, wrong entity: dev 'music streaming service I've been using lately': the Netflix sessions (-0.7) outrank the Spotify side remark (-3.4).

The gold user unit ranks below its own session's assistant echo (yoga rank 13, dog breed rank 11-15). Fixed by sweeping the session's user units and packing up to 5 user units of the cited session; without that, PA was 0.969.

Abstention misses: 'vintage films' passes the coverage check because 'film' appears in the camera session (abstain_p 0.15). Answerable questions with low logits ('painting of a sunset worth' -5.8, 'breed of my dog' -4.0) get a high abstain_p. dev AUC 0.90; on dev200 a single unanswerable question decides AUC.

Test audit: packs carry every drifting value (cat Sombra/Fig/Bica; starter Bubbles thinking / Bubbles / Herman saw / Masa renamed-latest) and possessor decoys (sister's favorite colour). The answer depends on Reactor following the own-statement and most-recent-wins hint.
core_requests: Answer-anchored citation in the pipeline: after Reactor answers, keep the cited passages that contain the answer, falling back to cite_plan. ssu gold is one session and packs deliberately hold decoys.

Make the all-role hybrid top-100 plus rerank the shared default pool (fully cached). Precompute a cache that reranks every user unit of the top-3 sessions so the session sweep is free; new rerank pairs cost about 40 s per question under contention.
build_pack option before_if_reply=True: render the previous assistant chunk only for short replies to a question (saves about 1.7k chars per question with no PA loss).
Model server: use separate locks or a priority for small /rerank batches; they currently queue behind large /embed batches from other agents.
next_ideas: Merge: B's retrieval and pack (all-role max-pool session ranking, user-unit sweep, 5 cited user units, conditional reply context, top-1 cite) with A's owner/polarity classifier as the tagger.
Tense feature: when the question is past tense ('was I', 'did I'), apply a soft penalty to plan/future units ('planning a trip', 'going to', 'next month'). This fixes the Japan cite.
Abstention by noun-phrase match instead of prefix match ('vintage films' vs 'vintage film cameras'), calibrated on dev and dev200 together (7 positives).
When the recency cue is present, force the latest head-term session into the pack (n_sess +2) so the newest value is never cut.
Trim other_units for sessions more than 8 logits below the top to save about 0.3k chars, if the test audit shows they never matter.

failure_patterns: Aggregate ago/since questions are parsed as a single event but need several sessions, so ALL fails: 'How many months have passed since I participated in two charity events in a row' (4 gold sessions, 1 packed); 'since I last visited a museum with a friend' (computed 5 is correct but 2 of 3 gold sessions are missing).

'first' questions get the right sessions (CF1=1.0) but miss a second gold turn in the same session (ATR=0.5): the necklace vs photo album question, the Ferrari model vs Zero fighter question. Variants sem_turns and sem_turns9 target this.
Event phrases too short to retrieve: 'a bus' / 'a train' put the gold at rank 35.
Whole-question route citation precision is low (CF1 0.58): a cite gap of 3 logits is too loose for single-answer questions such as 'cooking something for my friend a couple of days ago' (CF1 0.4).
Occasional wrong relative-date resolution: the flu recovery to 10th jog question computes 12 weeks against a gold of 15.
core_requests: Model-server throughput: precompute CE(question, hybrid top-100) for temporal questions on dev, dev200 and test, or add a per-client fair queue. Cold CE calls took 17-25 s under 13 concurrent sweeps. Also add progress lines to harness.sweep.
Temporal PA = ALL and (ATR==1 or HA==1), with HA reported separately, so that a correct computed gap is not penalised and a wrong one does not zero a perfect pack.
hx.rerank_texts(query, texts): sentence-level cross-encoder on arbitrary strings, cached by text hash.
next_ideas: Send aggregate questions ('last time', 'in a row', plurals, 'how many X before Y') to the whole-question route and compute the answer from the newest or oldest cited session.
Adaptive citation on the whole-question route: 1-2 sessions for single-answer questions, N for 'order of the N ...', a tighter logit gap otherwise.
Ablate sem_user at a 9k budget; adopt sem_turns9 (dev 75.3 / dev200 80.9) if the session user-turn fill holds up on its own.
Expand very short event phrases with question context before the CE.
Combine with lens A: their BM25 speed, holiday grammar and first-turn prior, with our CE decoy rejection (subject, contrast and year features).

failure_patterns: Old-value questions with several earlier candidates. 'previous personal best 5K' (dev200) cites the 27:12 run (not a personal best) instead of 27:45. The hint still lists all three statements, so only CF1 is lost.

Old-value partner with no lexical overlap. 'kitchen gadget before the Air Fryer' (dev): the 'my new Instant Pot' sentence shares no terms with 'gadget/invest'. The before-clause rule fixed the dev200 copy, where the wrong partner was later than the anchor.

Comparison questions. 'gym more frequently than previously': the new value ('four times a week') sits in a sentence about a smoothie; the cross-encoder prefers a sentence that contains 'more frequently'.
Two mentions of the same item. 'camera lens purchased most recently': two 70-200mm sentences compete and the more explicit one is in the wrong session.

Test audit: paraphrased updates without the attribute noun are not retrieved ('current job title' -> 'promotion ... Director of Clinical Services'). The old name one sentence before the attribute sentence is missed (skateboard 'Decaf'); the -1 sentence window fixes it but cost a dev200 pair, so it was rejected.
Abstention misses entity swaps where every question word exists in the history: 'Italian restaurants' (0.13), 'Software Engineer Manager' (0.09).
core_requests: hx.rerank_texts(query, texts): sentence-level cross-encoder through HistoryIndex. The lens calls core.models.rerank directly today, and that call was most of the cost under server contention.
Submission should honour cite_plan for KU (gold is always 2 sessions; the 2 extra context sessions would cost about 0.33 F1).
Expose b_semantic.analyze() / KU pair detection to the generic path (the router finds about 19% of dev KU). Same as lens A's request.
build_pack(pinned_uids=...) so the cited pair's units always enter the pack first.
Model-server queueing or priority: 16 concurrent sweeps made a 26-question dev200 run take 17 minutes; cached reruns take 5 seconds.
next_ideas: Phrase-level abstention: check bigrams like 'Italian restaurant(s)' and 'Engineer Manager' against the history instead of single terms, to catch entity swaps.
Old mode: choose the value immediately preceding the newest one among own same-attribute statements, instead of the strongest.
Attribute paraphrase expansion in the PRF hop (title -> promoted/role/position, instructor -> teach), borrowing lens A's synonym groups.
Gate the -1 sentence window on quoted or capitalised names only, to fix skateboard-style cases without the Lake Michigan bass regression.
Set computed = the newest pair value for numeric new-mode questions, if Reactor runs show the timeline hint is followed.

failure_patterns: Category word has no lexical or dense link to the instance ('projects led' -> 'case competition', 'poster'; 'health devices' -> 'hearing aids'). The gold unit never enters the hybrid pool or ranks 5th+ inside its own session, so the session or its gold turn is missing.

Depth-first (deep_top=8) packs only ~8-12 sessions on dev, so a 4th or 5th gold session is lost (magazine subscriptions; ALL drops from 1.0 to 0.984 on dev and 0.955 on dev200). It is still a net PA win over breadth-first.
The gold turn is an assistant turn (charity cycling: 'Congratulations on raising $250'), and only short assistant recaps are candidates.
Abstention is weak on dev (AUC 0.64) and decent on dev200 (0.83): a missing single facet ('30-gallon tank') is not detected reliably.
Test audit: the depth slots carry topical chit-chat units. That costs chars, and test counting questions with many instances (systolic > 130 in August) may need more breadth.
core_requests: Use cite_plan (or cite_plan intersected with Reactor's [E#]) as the final multi citations. The pack holds 8-17 sessions while gold has 2-5, so citing every passage drops CF1 from ~0.89 to ~0.5.
harness.failures should also print each gold turn's rank inside its own session (see scratch_b/atr_diag.py); that diagnostic exposed the per-session-cap problem.
Add an hx.rerank_sents / sentence-level cached CE helper, so test facts that are one sentence inside a 700-char unit are scored on their own.
Have the integrator run the generic baselines once per type and publish them. Agents A and B ran the identical generic baseline at the same time, which doubled the load on the shared model server.
next_ideas: Relevance floor for depth units (skip a unit whose CE logit is below top-8), with the saved chars going back into breadth for test-style repeated-measurement counts.
Choose depth vs breadth adaptively from how many sessions sit within 3 logits of the top CE score.
Sentence-level CE on the trimmed snippet, to improve ATR on test and catch category-to-instance misses.
Add A's facet/conjunct-absence check to abstain_p (facets are already parsed).
For 'days apart' (dates kind) questions, extract event dates and put the difference in computed, gated on Reactor spot checks.
Merge with lens A: A's lexical sweep and category LEXICON for recall, plus B's intra-session CE, deep_top depth and relative-CE cite plan.
